questions.wrongReply: Fashion sunglasses?! Blocking Jupiter's suns for style? The suns might take that personally!

questions.wrongReply: No hood?! With four suns, you'll never fall asleep! Unhooded sleepers become permanently jet lagged!

questions.officer: Have you registered this sleeping bag with Jupiter's sleep regulation authority?
questions.rightReply: Not registered yet! Don't worry, you can register at the sleep tax office. Just bring your pillow paperwork too!
questions.wrongReply: Already registered?! How?! You haven't even entered Jupiter yet! That's pre registration fraud!

questions.officer: Will you be sleeping outdoors on Jupiter?
questions.rightReply: Indoors only! Smart choice. Jupiter's outdoor winds would turn your sleeping bag into a hang glider!
questions.wrongReply: Sleeping outdoors?! The wind speeds here are 600 kilometres per hour! You'd wake up on Saturn!

questions.officer: A paint brush! Art is highly regulated on Jupiter. Do you have formal art training?
questions.rightReply: No training! Self expression is welcome on Jupiter. Untrained artists create the most interesting accidents!
questions.wrongReply: Formally trained?! Jupiter is suspicious of trained artists. They follow too many rules!

questions.officer: Is this paint brush clean right now?
questions.rightReply: Clean brush! A fresh start! Jupiter's art inspectors love a clean brush. No hidden paint agendas!
questions.wrongReply: Dirty brush?! What colour was it last?! Illegal pigments are a serious offence on Jupiter!

questions.officer: Do you plan to paint any Jupiter landscapes?
questions.rightReply: Landscape painting! Jupiter's scenery is breathtaking. Just don't paint the restricted military clouds!
questions.wrongReply: Not painting landscapes?! Then what?! Portraits of civilians without consent?! That's art crime!

questions.officer: Are the bristles made of natural hair?
questions.rightReply: Synthetic bristles! Jupiter's animal protection agency approves. No alien creatures were harmed!
questions.wrongReply: Natural hair?! From what animal?! Jupiter requires a hair source declaration for all natural bristle imports!

questions.officer: Will you clean this brush after every use?
questions.rightReply: Clean after every use! A responsible artist. Jupiter's drains can handle water based paint only!
questions.wrongReply: You won't clean it?! Dried paint on Jupiter crystallizes and becomes sharp! That's a safety hazard!

questions.officer: GLITTER?! Are you serious?! Do you know that glitter is classified as a biohazard on Jupiter?!
questions.rightReply: You didn't know! Glitter on Jupiter never goes away. The last glitter incident was three centuries ago and we're STILL finding it!
questions.wrongReply: You KNEW it's a biohazard and brought it anyway?! That's intentional contamination! Maximum alert!

questions.officer: Is this glitter the fine grain type?
questions.rightReply: Chunky glitter! At least chunky glitter is easier to clean up. Fine grain gets into EVERYTHING!
questions.wrongReply: Fine grain?! That's the worst kind! It gets into the atmosphere and creates sparkly storms for decades!

questions.officer: Is this glitter contained in a sealed container?
questions.rightReply: Sealed! Keep it that way! One unsealed glitter container could contaminate an entire Jupiter district!
questions.wrongReply: UNSEALED GLITTER?! This is a code red! Nobody move! One gust of wind and we're all sparkling for years!

questions.officer: Do you promise to use this glitter only in enclosed spaces?
questions.rightReply: Enclosed spaces only! Outdoor glitter use is punishable by 500 hours of community cleaning!
questions.wrongReply: Outdoor glitter?! You want to glitter bomb an entire planet?! We'd never recover from the sparkle!

questions.officer: Will you take all remaining glitter with you when you leave Jupiter?
questions.rightReply: Taking it all back! Thank you! Jupiter cannot handle any more permanent sparkle contamination!
questions.wrongReply: Leaving glitter behind?! That's littering with the most persistent substance in the universe!

questions.officer: A camera! Photography permits are required on Jupiter. Is this a digital camera?
questions.rightReply: Digital! Easy to delete embarrassing photos of Jupiter. Our tourism board appreciates digital!
questions.wrongReply: Film camera?! Physical evidence of Jupiter's secrets that can't be remotely deleted?! Very concerning!

questions.officer: Does this camera have a flash?
questions.rightReply: Flash equipped! Just don't use it near the wildlife. Jupiter's creatures are very camera shy!
questions.wrongReply: No flash?! So you're taking photos in the dark? What are you secretly photographing?!

questions.officer: Do you promise not to photograph any restricted Jupiter government buildings?
questions.rightReply: No government photos! Good. Our buildings are very self conscious about their architecture anyway!
questions.wrongReply: You want photos of government buildings?! Those buildings have privacy rights on Jupiter!

questions.officer: Is this camera worth more than 500 Jupiter credits?
questions.rightReply: Budget camera! Nothing fancy. No one steals cheap cameras, so you're safe from Jupiter's camera thieves!
questions.wrongReply: Expensive camera?! You'll attract every camera thief on Jupiter! They can smell expensive lenses!

questions.officer: Will you share your Jupiter photos on social media?
questions.rightReply: Sharing photos! Free advertising for Jupiter tourism! Our marketing department will be thrilled!
questions.wrongReply: Keeping them private?! What's the point of visiting Jupiter if you don't brag about it online?!

questions.officer: A frying pan! Jupiter's cooking competitions are legendary. Is this pan non stick?
questions.rightReply: Non stick! Essential on Jupiter where ingredients tend to bond with cookware permanently in the gravity!
questions.wrongReply: Not non stick?! In Jupiter's gravity, your food will fuse to the pan! You'll never separate them!

questions.officer: Is this frying pan cast iron?
questions.rightReply: Not cast iron! Good, because cast iron on Jupiter weighs about 200 kilograms. You'd need a crane to flip a pancake!
questions.wrongReply: Cast iron?! That thing weighs 200 kilos on Jupiter! Your arm would snap off trying to flip an egg!

questions.officer: Have you ever used this pan as a weapon?
questions.rightReply: Never used as a weapon! A peaceful pan with a clean culinary record!
questions.wrongReply: Pan combat veteran?! This is cookware, not a medieval shield! I'm reclassifying this as a weapon!

questions.officer: Do you plan to cook for Jupiter citizens?
questions.rightReply: Cooking for locals! Jupiter loves visitors who share their cuisine. You'll make friends instantly!
questions.wrongReply: Only cooking for yourself?! Selfish cooking is frowned upon on Jupiter! We believe in communal meals!

questions.officer: Is this pan oven safe?
questions.rightReply: Oven safe! Jupiter's ovens run at 3000 degrees. Your pan can probably handle at least some of that!
questions.wrongReply: Not oven safe?! Limited to stovetop only?! That severely restricts your cooking potential on Jupiter!

questions.officer: Hot sauce! Jupiter's food is notoriously bland. Is this hot sauce really spicy?
questions.rightReply: Very spicy! Jupiter citizens have never experienced spice. You'll be worshipped as a flavour deity!
questions.wrongReply: Mild?! Even our bland food is bolder than mild hot sauce! Why even bring it?!

questions.officer: Is this hot sauce in a glass bottle?
questions.rightReply: Glass bottle! Proper containment for dangerous flavour. Plastic would melt from the spice!
questions.wrongReply: Not glass?! What if the container dissolves from the spice?! Uncontained hot sauce is a hazard!

questions.officer: Have you declared the exact Scoville rating on your customs form?
questions.rightReply: Not declared! Rookie move, but we'll let it slide. Just don't surprise anyone with unexpected heat!
questions.wrongReply: You declared it?! Those numbers will trigger our heat alarm! We've never seen Scoville ratings before!

questions.officer: Do you promise to warn people before putting this on their food?
questions.rightReply: Warning before spicing! Very considerate. Unsuspecting Jupiter citizens have zero spice tolerance!
questions.wrongReply: No warning?! Surprise hot sauce is considered poisoning on Jupiter! They've never tasted spice before!

questions.officer: Is there more than one bottle in your bag?
questions.rightReply: Just one bottle! Personal spice supply. Completely legal and manageable!
questions.wrongReply: Multiple bottles?! That's enough to season the entire planet! You're basically a flavour arms dealer!

questions.officer: An apron! So you're a cook! Is this apron clean right now?
questions.rightReply: Clean apron! A fresh canvas for future food splatters. Jupiter's hygiene inspectors approve!
questions.wrongReply: Dirty apron?! That's walking evidence of unsanitary cooking practices! Jupiter's health code violation!

questions.officer: Does this apron have pockets?
questions.rightReply: Pockets! Perfect for holding spoons, secrets, and emergency snacks. Practical design!
questions.wrongReply: No pockets?! Where do you put your tasting spoon?! A pocketless apron is basically just a bib!

questions.officer: Is there anything written on this apron?
questions.rightReply: Blank apron! No controversial slogans. Jupiter's apron censorship board will be relieved!
questions.wrongReply: Text on the apron?! What does it say?! Unapproved apron slogans are a form of culinary propaganda!

questions.officer: Have you won any cooking competitions while wearing this apron?
questions.rightReply: No victories yet! An underdog! Jupiter loves a cooking underdog story. You might surprise everyone!
questions.wrongReply: A champion?! Professional chef alert! You'll have an unfair advantage in our amateur cooking scene!

questions.officer: Will you wear this apron at all times while cooking on Jupiter?
questions.rightReply: Apron at all times! Safety first! Jupiter kitchens are messy because of the gravity. Food flies everywhere!
questions.wrongReply: Cooking without an apron?! On Jupiter, the gravity makes food splatter everywhere! You'll be covered in sauce!

questions.officer: Flip flops! Jupiter's beaches have lava sand. Are these heat resistant?
questions.rightReply: Heat resistant! You came prepared for Jupiter's volcanic beaches. Your toes will thank you!
questions.wrongReply: Not heat resistant?! Jupiter's beach sand is 400 degrees! Your flip flops would melt in seconds!

questions.officer: Do these flip flops make that slapping sound when you walk?
questions.rightReply: Silent flip flops! Jupiter's beach noise pollution laws are very strict. You're already in compliance!
questions.wrongReply: Slappy flip flops?! On Jupiter's beaches, that sound attracts the sand crabs! They LOVE that rhythm!

questions.officer: Are these the kind with the strap between your toes?
questions.rightReply: Toe strap style! Classic design. Jupiter's toe fashion critics consider this timeless!
questions.wrongReply: No toe strap?! Those are just slides! Slides on Jupiter's gravity are slippery chaos waiting to happen!

questions.officer: Have you ever lost a flip flop in the ocean?
questions.rightReply: Never lost one! Responsible footwear ownership! Lost flip flops become hazards for Jupiter's sea creatures!
questions.wrongReply: Lost in the ocean?! Jupiter's sea creatures would attach it to their collection of Earth artifacts!

questions.officer: Will you wear these only at the beach?
questions.rightReply: Beach only! Flip flops in Jupiter's cities are frowned upon. Too casual for our sophisticated streets!
questions.wrongReply: Wearing them everywhere?! Flip flops at a Jupiter restaurant?! The dress code police will arrest your feet!

questions.officer: A snorkel! Jupiter's oceans are made of liquid metallic hydrogen. Can you swim in metal?
questions.rightReply: Can't swim in metal! At least you're honest. Most tourists lie and then sink immediately!
questions.wrongReply: You can swim in metal?! That's physically impossible! Are you made of something I should know about?!

questions.officer: Is this snorkel a standard breathing tube?
questions.rightReply: Standard tube! Nothing fancy. It won't work in liquid metal anyway, but at least it's not suspicious!
questions.wrongReply: Modified snorkel?! What modifications?! Are you trying to breathe in our metallic oceans?! That's not possible!

questions.officer: Do you have a mask to go with this snorkel?
questions.rightReply: Full set! A prepared snorkeler. Even if Jupiter's oceans are unswimmable, you've got the spirit!
questions.wrongReply: No mask?! A snorkel without a mask is just a tube! What are you going to do, breathe through it on land?!

questions.officer: Have you ever seen a fish through this snorkel?
questions.rightReply: Fish experience! Jupiter's fish are the size of buildings, so you won't need a snorkel to see them!
questions.wrongReply: Never seen a fish?! Then you've never actually used this properly! What have you been snorkeling in?!

questions.officer: Will you accept that Jupiter snorkeling is purely decorative?
questions.rightReply: Decorative snorkeling accepted! Tourists who wear snorkels on land are a beloved Jupiter tradition!
questions.wrongReply: You want functional snorkeling?! In liquid metal?! I admire your ambition but question your judgment!

questions.officer: A beach ball! On Jupiter's gravity, this will weigh as much as a bowling ball. Is it fully inflated?
questions.rightReply: Deflated! Smart! An inflated beach ball on Jupiter would be impossible to catch without breaking a finger!
questions.wrongReply: Fully inflated?! The pressure difference will make this thing dense as a rock! You'll shatter a window!

questions.officer: Is this beach ball multicoloured?
questions.rightReply: Multicoloured! The official colour scheme of Jupiter tourism. You're basically carrying a welcome sign!
questions.wrongReply: Single colour?! Plain beach balls are boring and Jupiter's beaches demand visual excitement!

questions.officer: Do you plan to play beach volleyball with this?
questions.rightReply: No volleyball! Good, because spiking a Jupiter heavy beach ball would put someone in the hospital!
questions.wrongReply: Volleyball?! With Jupiter gravity, a spike would go through the sand and into the planet's core!

questions.officer: Have you written your name on this beach ball?
questions.rightReply: Named beach ball! Smart, because on Jupiter's beaches, light objects blow away to other continents!
questions.wrongReply: Unnamed?! An anonymous beach ball is a lost beach ball on Jupiter. The wind will claim it immediately!

questions.officer: Will you keep this beach ball away from Jupiter's atmosphere vents?
questions.rightReply: Away from vents! One vent gust and this ball would launch into space! You'd never see it again!
questions.wrongReply: Near the vents?! That ball would become a satellite! Jupiter would have a new tiny colourful moon!

questions.officer: A neck tie! On Jupiter, ties are worn around the waist as belts. Will you wear it correctly?
questions.rightReply: Wearing it as a belt! You'll fit right in with Jupiter's fashion scene. Very professional waist!
questions.wrongReply: Around the neck?! AROUND THE NECK?! That's considered wildly inappropriate on Jupiter! Cover your neck immediately!

questions.officer: Is this tie made of silk?
questions.rightReply: Not silk! Good, because Jupiterian silk worms would sense it and become very territorial!
questions.wrongReply: Silk?! Jupiter's giant silk worms will swarm you! They're very protective of their fabric monopoly!

questions.officer: Is this tie patterned?
questions.rightReply: Patterned! Jupiter fashion values complexity. Solid colours are for rookies and robots!
questions.wrongReply: Solid colour?! That's the most boring fashion choice possible on Jupiter. You'll be the outfit equivalent of beige!

questions.officer: Do you know how to tie at least three knot styles?
questions.rightReply: Limited knot knowledge! That's fine, Jupiter only recognizes one knot: the reverse loop. We'll teach you!
questions.wrongReply: Three knots?! Showoff! On Jupiter, we use one knot for everything. Simplicity is elegance!

questions.officer: Will you remove this tie when eating?
questions.rightReply: Removing when eating! Smart, because Jupiter food is messy and ties absorb sauce like sponges!
questions.wrongReply: Eating with a tie on?! That tie will become a flavour journal of every meal! Stain city!

questions.officer: A briefcase! Very professional. Does this briefcase have a lock?
questions.rightReply: Locked briefcase! Security conscious! Jupiter's corporate world respects a locked briefcase!
questions.wrongReply: No lock?! Anyone could peek inside! Jupiter's corporate spies are everywhere and they love unlocked briefcases!

questions.officer: Is there anything important inside this briefcase?
questions.rightReply: Nothing important! An empty ish briefcase carried for appearances. Jupiter's business pros do the same thing!
questions.wrongReply: Important stuff?! Then why isn't it locked?! Oh wait, it is. But what KIND of important?! Now I'm curious!

questions.officer: Is this briefcase leather?
questions.rightReply: Not leather! Jupiter's synthetic material industry will be pleased. They're trying to corner the market!
questions.wrongReply: Real leather?! From what creature?! Jupiter requires a species origin report for all animal based products!

questions.officer: Have you ever accidentally left this briefcase somewhere?
questions.rightReply: Never lost! An attentive briefcase owner. On Jupiter, abandoned briefcases trigger bomb squad evacuations!
questions.wrongReply: You've left it behind?! On Jupiter, that triggers a full security lockdown! The bomb squad gets very excited!

questions.officer: Will you be bringing this briefcase to your interview?
questions.rightReply: Bringing it to the interview! Professional appearance matters! Jupiter employers judge briefcase quality first!
questions.wrongReply: Not bringing it?! Then you'll carry your Jupiter resume in your hands like some kind of amateur!

questions.officer: Breath mints! On Jupiter, mint scent is considered a luxury perfume. Are these extra strong?
questions.rightReply: Extra strong! You'll smell like a walking luxury boutique on Jupiter. People will follow you around!
questions.wrongReply: Weak mints?! Those barely register on Jupiter's scent scale. You'll need at least 50 at once!

questions.officer: Are these sugar free?
questions.rightReply: Sugar free! Jupiter's dental insurance doesn't cover sugar damage. Smart financial decision!
questions.wrongReply: Contains sugar?! Jupiter's dentists charge 1000 credits per cavity! You're basically eating money!

questions.officer: Do you have more than 20 mints?
questions.rightReply: Under 20! Personal breath supply. Completely within Jupiter's mint possession limits!
questions.wrongReply: Over 20?! That exceeds the personal mint limit! You'd need a mint distribution license for that many!

questions.officer: Will you offer mints to your interviewer?
questions.rightReply: Sharing mints with the interviewer! Jupiter interview etiquette says mint sharing shows confidence and generosity!
questions.wrongReply: Not sharing?! On Jupiter, refusing to share mints in an interview is the same as saying 'I don't trust your breath!'

questions.officer: Do these mints come in a metal tin?
questions.rightReply: Metal tin! The satisfying click of a mint tin is considered a power move on Jupiter. Click away!
questions.wrongReply: No tin?! Loose mints in a bag?! That's chaotic energy that Jupiter interviewers do NOT appreciate!

questions.officer: A balloon! On Jupiter's gravity, balloons don't float. They just sit on the ground sadly. Is this balloon inflated?
questions.rightReply: Deflated! Good thinking bringing it flat. You can inflate it with Jupiter helium, which makes balloons talk!
questions.wrongReply: Already inflated?! Earth air inside a balloon on Jupiter just sits there depressed. It won't float at all!

questions.officer: Is this balloon a festive colour?
questions.rightReply: Festive! Jupiter birthday parties are massive celebrations. Your balloon will fit right in!
questions.wrongReply: A boring coloured balloon?! Birthday parties on Jupiter require maximum colour saturation! Step it up!

questions.officer: Do you know how to make balloon animals?
questions.rightReply: No balloon animals! That's fine, Jupiter has real animals at parties. They're more fun anyway!
questions.wrongReply: Balloon animals?! Jupiter children find them terrifying! Twisted rubber creatures give them nightmares!

questions.officer: Will you be using this balloon as a party decoration?
questions.rightReply: Party decoration! The most noble purpose for a balloon. Jupiter approves of your decorating plans!
questions.wrongReply: Not a decoration?! What else do you do with a balloon?! Non decorative balloon use is very suspicious!

questions.officer: Are you prepared for the possibility that this balloon might pop in Jupiter's atmosphere?
questions.rightReply: Prepared for popping! Jupiter's atmospheric pressure is unpredictable. Brave balloon ownership!
questions.wrongReply: Not prepared?! Jupiter pops balloons without warning! The sound echoes for miles! Emotional damage guaranteed!

questions.officer: A party hat! On Jupiter, party hats are considered formal headwear. Is this a pointy cone hat?
questions.rightReply: Pointy cone! The most prestigious hat shape on Jupiter. You'll outrank most government officials!
questions.wrongReply: Not pointy?! Flat party hats are considered casual and insulting at Jupiter celebrations!

questions.officer: Does this party hat have an elastic chin strap?
questions.rightReply: Chin strap! Essential on Jupiter. Without it, the wind would launch your hat into the next time zone!
questions.wrongReply: No chin strap?! That hat will fly off in Jupiter's winds and hit someone! Unsecured hat violation!

questions.officer: Is this party hat sparkly?
questions.rightReply: Not sparkly! Thank goodness. After the glitter incident of 2547, Jupiter banned all sparkly headwear!
questions.wrongReply: Sparkly?! Have you learned nothing from the Great Glitter Disaster?! Sparkles on Jupiter never come off!

questions.officer: Have you worn this hat to another party before?
questions.rightReply: First time hat! Virgin party hat. Jupiter believes every party deserves a fresh hat. Respect!
questions.wrongReply: A used hat?! Recycled party energy is considered bad luck on Jupiter! Fresh hats only!

questions.officer: Will you wear this hat for the entire duration of the party?
questions.rightReply: Full party commitment! Removing your hat mid party on Jupiter is like leaving before the cake. Unthinkable!
questions.wrongReply: Taking it off early?! That's a party foul of the highest order on Jupiter! Hat removal means party betrayal!

questions.officer: Candles?! On a gas planet?! Are you trying to blow us all up?! Are these real wax candles?
questions.rightReply: Not real wax! LED candles? Battery powered? Smart! The fakest flames possible! Jupiter approves!
questions.wrongReply: REAL WAX CANDLES?! With ACTUAL FIRE?! On a planet made of FLAMMABLE GAS?! Are you insane?!

questions.officer: Are these birthday candles?
questions.rightReply: Birthday candles! Tiny, brief, and specific to cake. The least dangerous candle category!
questions.wrongReply: Regular candles?! Those burn for HOURS! One gust of Jupiter wind into a regular flame and we're all done!

questions.officer: Do you have a way to light these without an open flame?
questions.rightReply: Flameless ignition! Electric lighter? Perfect! Jupiter's fire department just breathed a sigh of relief!
questions.wrongReply: Open flame lighter?! A lighter on Jupiter?! That's basically a detonator! Hand it over immediately!

questions.officer: Is there someone at this party who can blow them out quickly?
questions.rightReply: Quick blower available! Speed is everything when candles are lit on Jupiter. Three seconds maximum!
questions.wrongReply: No one to blow them out quickly?! Lingering flames on Jupiter are an extinction level event!

questions.officer: Do you accept full responsibility for any fire related incidents?
questions.rightReply: Full responsibility accepted! Brave. Jupiter's insurance rates for candle accidents are astronomical!
questions.wrongReply: No responsibility?! Then who's liable when the atmosphere ignites?! Someone has to sign the waiver!

questions.officer: A compass! Jupiter has 79 magnetic poles. Your compass is going to spin like crazy. Did you know that?
questions.rightReply: Didn't know! Don't worry, everyone's compass goes haywire here. It's actually entertaining to watch!
questions.wrongReply: You knew?! And you still brought a useless spinning needle?! What's your plan, get dizzy watching it?!

questions.officer: Is this a traditional magnetic compass?
questions.rightReply: Magnetic! It'll spin like a fidget spinner with 79 poles pulling it everywhere. Fun toy at least!
questions.wrongReply: Digital compass?! Digital compasses explode near Jupiter's magnetic fields! Don't turn that thing on!

questions.officer: Do you actually plan to navigate with this on Jupiter?
questions.rightReply: Not for navigation! Smart. Using a compass on Jupiter is like using a map in a tornado. Pointless!
questions.wrongReply: Navigate with this?! You'll walk in 79 different directions simultaneously! You'll end up going in circles!

questions.officer: Is this compass made of metal?
questions.rightReply: Metal compass! The magnetic fields will make it stick to random surfaces. Keep it in your pocket!
questions.wrongReply: Not metal?! Then it's not a real compass! Wait, that actually makes it safer on Jupiter!

questions.officer: Will you keep this compass as a souvenir rather than a navigation tool?
questions.rightReply: Souvenir status! A compass that points everywhere is actually a great conversation starter!
questions.wrongReply: Using it for real?! I'm telling you, it points in 79 directions at once! You'll be more lost than when you started!

questions.officer: Binoculars! Jupiter has strict anti peeping laws. Are these for birdwatching?
questions.rightReply: Birdwatching! Jupiter's birds are the size of cars, so you won't actually need these, but the intent is pure!
questions.wrongReply: Not birdwatching?! Then what are you going to stare at from far away?! That's suspicious long distance looking!

questions.officer: Are these binoculars high magnification?
questions.rightReply: Low magnification! You can barely see far with these. Harmless peeping equipment! Wait, I mean observation tools!
questions.wrongReply: High magnification?! You could see into someone's living room from another continent! Privacy violation alert!

questions.officer: Do these binoculars have night vision?
questions.rightReply: No night vision! Not that it matters, Jupiter has four suns so there IS no night! Basic optics only!
questions.wrongReply: Night vision?! There's no night on Jupiter with four suns! What are you planning to see in darkness that doesn't exist?!

questions.officer: Have you ever used these binoculars at a Jupiter distance of more than 10 kilometres?
questions.rightReply: Short range only! Responsible observation distance. Jupiter's privacy laws allow up to 5 kilometres!
questions.wrongReply: Long range observation?! That's basically spying! Jupiter's counter espionage agency will want to speak with you!

questions.officer: Will you wear these around your neck as a fashion accessory?
questions.rightReply: Neck binoculars! Very tourist chic on Jupiter. Everyone will know you're here for a good time!
questions.wrongReply: Hiding them?! Hidden binoculars suggest sneaky observation! Wear them proudly or not at all!

questions.officer: Rope! That's an unusual travel item. Is this rope less than 10 metres long?
questions.rightReply: Short rope! Personal use length. Good for tying things together and not much else. Harmless!
questions.wrongReply: Over 10 metres?! That's industrial rope! What are you planning to tie up that needs THAT much rope?!

questions.officer: Can you tie any knots?
questions.rightReply: Knot knowledge! A useful skill on Jupiter where everything needs to be tied down because of the gravity!
questions.wrongReply: Can't tie knots?! Then what good is the rope?! It's just a floppy line that does nothing! Useless!

questions.officer: Is this rope for climbing purposes?
questions.rightReply: Not for climbing! Good, because Jupiter's cliffs are made of gas. You can't climb gas, no matter how good your rope is!
questions.wrongReply: Climbing?! Jupiter's mountains are gas formations! You'd fall right through them! Climbing is impossible here!

questions.officer: Have you ever used this rope to tie someone up?
questions.rightReply: No tying history! A clean rope with no criminal bindings on its record. This rope is innocent!
questions.wrongReply: You've tied someone up?! This rope has a history! I need to run a background check on this rope!

questions.officer: Will you keep this rope coiled neatly at all times?
questions.rightReply: Neatly coiled! Loose rope on Jupiter is a tripping hazard multiplied by extreme gravity. Safety first!
questions.wrongReply: Uncoiled rope?! In Jupiter's gravity, loose rope becomes a tangled trap that nobody can escape from!

questions.officer: Popcorn! Jupiter's cinemas serve rocks instead of popcorn. Earth popcorn is considered exotic here! Is it buttered?
questions.rightReply: Buttered! The most luxurious form of Earth snack. Jupiter's movie goers will be so jealous!
questions.wrongReply: No butter?! Dry popcorn is considered a punishment snack on Jupiter! Even rocks are buttered here!

questions.officer: Is this popcorn freshly popped?
questions.rightReply: Fresh popcorn! The smell alone will cause a crowd of curious Jupiter citizens to gather around you!
questions.wrongReply: Stale popcorn?! That's basically just sad corn! It had one job and it did it too long ago!

questions.officer: Is there enough popcorn to share with the person next to you in the cinema?
questions.rightReply: Enough to share! Jupiter cinema etiquette demands you share with your seat neighbours. Generous popcorn carrier!
questions.wrongReply: Not enough to share?! Solo popcorn eating at Jupiter cinemas is considered extremely antisocial!

questions.officer: Did you add any extra seasoning to this popcorn?
questions.rightReply: No extra seasoning! Pure classic popcorn. Jupiter's taste buds can barely handle butter as it is!
questions.wrongReply: Extra seasoning?! Jupiter citizens have never tasted Earth seasoning! One kernel could overwhelm their taste buds!

questions.officer: Will you try not to make too much crunching noise during the movie?
questions.rightReply: Quiet cruncher! Jupiter movie theatres amplify sound, so a loud crunch echoes for the entire movie!
questions.wrongReply: Loud crunching?! Jupiter's acoustic atmosphere means your crunching would drown out the movie dialogue!

questions.officer: 3D glasses! Jupiter's movies are already in 5D, so these are actually under qualified. Are these the cinema kind?
questions.rightReply: Cinema 3D glasses! Cute. They'll downgrade your Jupiter 5D movie experience, but they're harmless!
questions.wrongReply: Custom 3D glasses?! Modified optics could interfere with Jupiter's 5D projection technology! Risky!

questions.officer: Do these glasses have red and blue lenses?
questions.rightReply: Modern 3D glasses! No red and blue. That ancient technology would make Jupiter movies look like abstract art!
questions.wrongReply: Red and blue lenses?! Those are museum pieces! Jupiter hasn't used that technology in 400 years!

questions.officer: Did you take these from an Earth cinema without returning them?
questions.rightReply: A cinema souvenir thief! On Jupiter, that's actually considered resourceful. We respect frugality!
questions.wrongReply: You bought your own?! Who BUYS 3D glasses?! Jupiter's economists are bewildered by this decision!

questions.officer: Will you wear these glasses outside the cinema?
questions.rightReply: Cinema use only! Smart, because wearing 3D glasses outside on Jupiter makes everything look fake!
questions.wrongReply: Wearing them everywhere?! The world looked 3D already! You'll just get a headache and walk into things!

questions.officer: Do you accept that Jupiter's 5D experience might blow your mind?
questions.rightReply: Mind blowing accepted! Jupiter's 5D engages senses you didn't even know you had! Prepare yourself!
questions.wrongReply: Not prepared?! Jupiter's 5D once made a tourist forget their own name for three hours! It's intense!

questions.officer: An autograph book! Jupiter has many celebrities. Is this book mostly empty?
questions.rightReply: Mostly empty! Room for Jupiter's biggest stars! Our celebrities love signing things for tourists!
questions.wrongReply: Already full?! No room for Jupiter autographs?! Our celebrities will be deeply offended!

questions.officer: Do you have a pen to go with this book?
questions.rightReply: Pen ready! Prepared autograph hunter. Jupiter's celebrities hate when fans ask to borrow their pens!
questions.wrongReply: No pen?! You'll ask a celebrity for their pen?! That's the fastest way to get ignored on Jupiter!

questions.officer: Are you going to ask any Jupiter customs officers for their autograph?
questions.rightReply: Customs officer autograph! Nobody EVER asks us! You just made my day! Let me find my good pen!
questions.wrongReply: Not asking us?! Customs officers are the first celebrities you meet! We're basically the gatekeepers of fame!

questions.officer: Is this autograph book hardcover?
questions.rightReply: Hardcover! Durable and professional. Jupiter's celebrities only sign hardcover books. It's in their contracts!
questions.wrongReply: Softcover?! Jupiter celebrities will crumple it while signing! Hardcover is the minimum standard!

questions.officer: Will you get this autograph book signed by at least 10 Jupiter celebrities?
questions.rightReply: At least 10! Jupiter has hundreds of celebrities. With that ambition, you'll need a second book!
questions.wrongReply: Less than 10?! You're on Jupiter, the planet of stars! Set your autograph goals higher!
